schema.articleDescription: How to use 4-7-8 breathing to overcome insomnia naturally. Dr. Weil's technique that works in 2-5 minutes.
schema.faq.items.0.answer: Yes, 4-7-8 breathing is one of the most effective natural techniques for insomnia. The extended exhale (8 counts) activates your parasympathetic nervous system, slowing your heart rate and signaling your body it's safe to sleep. Dr. Andrew Weil, who popularized the technique, calls it a 'natural tranquilizer' that becomes more effective with regular practice.
schema.faq.items.0.question: Does 4-7-8 breathing really help with insomnia?
schema.faq.items.1.answer: Start with 4 cycles (about 1 minute) when you get into bed. Most people start feeling drowsy within 2-4 cycles. If you're still awake after 4 cycles, rest for 30 seconds and do another 4 cycles. Dr. Weil recommends not exceeding 8 cycles in one session when you're new to the technique.
schema.faq.items.1.question: How many cycles of 4-7-8 should I do for insomnia?
schema.faq.items.2.answer: 4-7-8 works for sleep through three mechanisms: (1) the long exhale activates the vagus nerve, triggering relaxation, (2) the breath hold allows CO2 to build slightly, which has a calming effect, and (3) the counting gives your mind a single focus, interrupting racing thoughts that keep you awake.
schema.faq.items.2.question: Why does 4-7-8 breathing work for sleep?

sections.why.paragraph1: If you've ever lain awake at 2 AM with a racing mind, you know how frustrating insomnia can be. Your body is tired but your nervous system is stuck in “alert mode”, the sympathetic fight-or-flight state that evolved to keep our ancestors safe from predators.
